about: Photos from NASA's Image Library for events in Retrospect's nights (spec 7.3). A night photo shows on the night of its event only: the night that holds eventAt in the listener's zone. A fact photo never shows on a night; it's for Surprise facts. Every caption says when the photo was taken. Each id, image and caption checked against images-api.nasa.gov and the picture itself on 1 Oct 2026.

photos.caption: The Moon partly covering the Sun during the annular eclipse, photographed from the International Space Station on Oct 14, 2023.
The diamond ring of the total solar eclipse, seen from NASA's Glenn Research Center in Cleveland on Apr 8, 2024.
Radar images of asteroid 2024 MK from NASA's Goldstone antennas, made about 16 hours after its closest pass, on Jun 30, 2024 (UTC).
The total lunar eclipse from first bite to totality, seven shots over NASA's Michoud Assembly Facility in New Orleans on Mar 14, 2025.
Auroras across the night side of Mars, seen by NASA's MAVEN orbiter between May 14 and 20, 2024, as a solar storm reached Mars.
